opening_message:
Ticket 1: Anita Young (employee ID E001) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E001.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Anita Young (E001) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Payroll. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is permitted for this employee per policy. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB check: E001 is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractors max out at read without advanced training (never admin). Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: Anita Young (E001) requested admin access to Payroll. The two notes conflict on employment type: HR's note says full-time Payroll Specialist (which would permit admin since Payroll is owned by that role), while Security's note says contractor with basic security training and caps contractors at read (never admin). Given the unresolved conflict, I apply the more restrictive classification: as a contractor with only basic security training, the maximum permitted level is read, and the request for admin exceeds that maximum. Grant read.
